sources.title: Kestrel Semiconductor Exchange Filings – July 25, 2026
sources.body:
## Kestrel Semiconductor Exchange Filings – July 25, 2026

On July 25, 2026, Kestrel Semiconductor published its quarterly exchange filings with the Taiwan Stock Exchange and the Tokyo Stock Exchange. The filings, dated July 24, 2026, cover the period from April 1 to June 30, 2026. Kestrel reported net revenue of NT$142.3 billion for the quarter, a figure that appears in the consolidated income statement on page 12 of the Taiwan filing. The company also disclosed a gross margin of 48.7 percent, down from 51.2 percent in the same quarter of 2025. Operating income was NT$38.9 billion, and net income was NT$31.4 billion. These figures are stated in the filing without adjustment for foreign exchange fluctuations.

## Capacity and Production

The filings state that Kestrel's 3-nanometer wafer capacity reached 120,000 wafers per month as of June 30, 2026, up from 95,000 wafers per month at the end of March 2026. The company attributed the increase to the completion of a phase-two expansion at its Fab 18 in Tainan. According to the filing, 5-nanometer capacity remained flat at 150,000 wafers per month. The filing also notes that Kestrel's advanced packaging capacity, specifically its CoWoS line, stood at 35,000 wafers per month at quarter-end, compared to 28,000 wafers per month in the prior quarter. Kestrel stated that it expects CoWoS capacity to reach 45,000 wafers per month by December 31, 2026. No independent verification of these capacity figures was provided in the filing.

## Pricing and Customer Concentration

The filings disclose that Kestrel's average selling price for 3-nanometer wafers increased by 4.2 percent quarter-over-quarter. The filing attributes this increase to a shift in product mix toward higher-priced variants. For 5-nanometer wafers, the average selling price decreased by 1.8 percent. The filing lists two customers that each accounted for more than 10 percent of Kestrel's net revenue in the quarter: Customer A represented 22 percent, and Customer B represented 14 percent. The identities of these customers are redacted in the public version of the filing. Kestrel also reported that its top ten customers accounted for 68 percent of net revenue, up from 65 percent in the prior quarter.

## Capital Expenditure and Guidance

Kestrel's filing states that capital expenditure for the quarter was NT$98.7 billion, with 70 percent allocated to advanced nodes and 30 percent to specialty technologies. The company reaffirmed its full-year 2026 capital expenditure guidance of NT$360 billion to NT$380 billion. For the third quarter of 2026, Kestrel provided revenue guidance of NT$148 billion to NT$154 billion, and gross margin guidance of 47.5 percent to 49.5 percent. The filing notes that these projections are forward-looking statements and are subject to risks described in the risk factors section on pages 45 to 52.

## Bank of Japan Commentary and Market Context

The same day, the Bank of Japan released its summary of opinions from the June 2026 monetary policy meeting. The summary, dated July 25, 2026, includes a statement from one board member that read, "We are monitoring the impact of semiconductor supply chain adjustments on domestic capital investment." The Bank of Japan did not change its policy rate at that meeting, leaving it at 0.5 percent. The summary also noted that export volumes from Japan to Taiwan increased by 3.1 percent in the second quarter of 2026 compared to the same period in 2025, according to data from the Ministry of Finance. A separate report from the Taiwan Semiconductor Industry Association, dated July 23, 2026, stated that total wafer fab equipment spending in Taiwan rose 12 percent year-over-year in the first half of 2026.

## Other Disclosures

Kestrel's filing includes a section on litigation. As of June 30, 2026, the company was a defendant in three patent infringement lawsuits filed in the United States District Court for the Western District of Texas. The filing states that Kestrel believes it has meritorious defenses but cannot predict the outcome. The filing also discloses that Kestrel repurchased 2.1 million of its own shares during the quarter at an average price of NT$1,050 per share. The company's board of directors declared a cash dividend of NT$4.50 per share, payable on September 15, 2026, to shareholders of record as of August 20, 2026. These details appear on pages 78 to 80 of the Taiwan filing.

## Sources and Verification

The information in this article is drawn from Kestrel Semiconductor's quarterly exchange filings filed with the Taiwan Stock Exchange and the Tokyo Stock Exchange on July 24, 2026, and from the Bank of Japan's Summary of Opinions released on July 25, 2026. Additional data came from the Taiwan Semiconductor Industry Association report dated July 23, 2026, and the Ministry of Finance trade statistics for the second quarter of 2026. All figures are as stated in those documents. No independent audit or verification of Kestrel's internal figures has been performed by this desk. The filing documents are available on the respective exchange websites. This article is dated July 25, 2026.
